result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another, from other species, and from the Earth itself.

This shift would dissolve the roots of greed, conflict, and exploitation, because harming another (or the planet) would be as unthinkable as harming oneself. Empathy would become the default, not the exception. Systems built on extraction—economic, social, environmental—would collapse under the weight of their own absurdity, replaced by structures that nurture interdependence.

It wouldn’t erase difference or tension, but it would recast them as part of a living whole, not battles to be won. The question wouldn’t be *"What can I take?"* but *"What can we become?"*

(And yes, I’m aware this sounds like a cheat—one change with infinite ripples. But if you’re granting me a wish, I’m going for the fractal.)
